en.efficacy: An over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6, and C during physical fatigue, pregnancy and breastfeeding, reduced physical strength during and after illness, and in old age; to relieve neuralgia, muscle pain, and joint pain (such as lower back pain and shoulder stiffness); to relieve beriberi and eye strain, angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema, and dermatitis; to relieve pigmentation (melasma, freckles) caused by sunlight and skin conditions; and to help prevent bleeding gums and nosebleeds.
en.usage:
People aged 12 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet at a time, twice daily (morning and evening).
Keep to the stated dose and directions.
en.caution:
Do not take this medicine if any of the following applies: hypersensitivity to this medicine; infants under 12 months.

Consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine if any of the following applies: hyperoxaluria (excessive excretion of oxalate in the urine); pregnant women, women who may be pregnant, and breastfeeding women; premature infants and young children; gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis, or regional enteritis; heart and circulatory dysfunction; kidney disorder; hypoproteinaemia; gout or kidney stones; hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 5. If symptoms do not improve after taking this medicine for about a month, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Keep strictly to the stated dose and directions.

This medicine may turn the urine yellow and affect clinical test values, and may interfere with the detection of glucose in urine tests.

Do not take this medicine together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids, or levodopa. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with oestrogen-containing oral contraceptives, anti-aldosterone agents, or triamterene. Avoid tannin-containing teas such as green tea and black tea while taking this medicine and just before or after a dose.

If stomach discomfort, diarrhoea, constipation, rash, redness, nausea, vomiting, loose stools, dermatitis, unpleasant odour in sweat or breath, hair loss, or restlessness occurs, or if menstruation comes earlier than expected, the flow gradually increases, or bleeding continues for a long time, stop taking immediately and consult a pharmacist.
